program_name: Area and Global Studies for International Cooperation (AGIC)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught (case 1). The entire 2-year, 120-ECTS Laurea Magistrale is delivered in English; UNITO's official degree record lists 'Language: English' and the apply.unito.it course page lists 'Study language: English'. It is a single UNITO degree awarded by the Department of Cultures, Politics and Society - NOT an English pathway inside an Italian-named programme and NOT an interuniversity/joint degree (the programme has partnerships with African, American, Latin American and Asian universities and research centres, but these are cooperation agreements, not a joint-degree structure). Important nuance: although teaching is in English, the programme requires students to also acquire/possess a SECOND language at CEFR A2 or above (French, Portuguese, Spanish, Swahili, Arabic, Hindi, Chinese, Russian, Japanese - or Italian for international students), and second-year area-profile courses include language modules. International students are additionally expected to have basic Italian (A2), or to take an Italian course. So the degree is English-medium but explicitly multilingual in its requirements.
campus: Turin (Torino), Piedmont, Italy. Official 'Headquarter: TORINO'. Administering structure: Department of Cultures, Politics and Society (Dipartimento di Culture, Politica e Societa), School of Law, Political and Economic-Social Sciences - teaching is based at the Campus Luigi Einaudi, Lungo Dora Siena 100, Turin. [uncertain]
degree_class: LM-81 R - Scienze per la cooperazione allo sviluppo (Development Co-operation). UNITO programme code: 0308M23. Per the programme's Key Information page the classification is LM-81 for cohort 2024 and previous cohorts, and LM-81 R from cohort 2025 onwards (the '-R' suffix reflects the 2025 reform of the Italian degree classes). CINECA course-catalogue id: 12444.
admission_type: Open access / free admission with a required admission interview ('corso ad accesso non programmato' - the official UNITO record states Access: Free). There is no numerus clausus and no national/TOLC-style entrance test, but enrolment is possible ONLY after passing an individual interview ('colloquio') that verifies curricular requirements and the adequacy of the candidate's personal preparation. Access is therefore 'open access + selection call/interview' rather than purely open. Reserved international quota: 60 places for non-EU citizens residing abroad, plus 10 places reserved for Marco Polo programme students. Candidates with a foreign qualification must go through the Apply@UniTo portal; candidates with an Italian qualification register for the interview through MyUniTo. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: For a.y. 2026/2027, applicants with a FOREIGN qualification (including EU citizens and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy) apply via Apply@UniTo: First admission call (postgraduate degree programmes, open to ALL applicants): 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026. A second window for free-access postgraduate programmes, reserved to Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, ran 25 August - 8 September 2026 (numbered the 'Fourth admission call' on apply.unito.it and the 'Second application call for free access postgraduate programs' on en.unito.it - the two official pages number the calls differently). Applicants holding an ITALIAN qualification do not use Apply@UniTo: they register for the AGIC admission interview through MyUniTo, within the interview-session registration windows published each year on the programme's 'How to apply' page (for a.y. 2023/2024 there were three sessions between June and September, plus a make-up session in October; the specific 2026/2027 session dates could not be retrieved because agic.unito.it is unreachable). [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU citizens residing abroad (visa applicants) for a.y. 2026/2027: apply through Apply@UniTo in the First admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 (this is the only Apply@UniTo call open to non-EU applicants residing abroad for postgraduate programmes; the later calls are explicitly reserved to Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy). In addition, the pre-enrolment (study visa) application must be submitted on the Universitaly platform by 15 July 2026. The apply.unito.it course page for AGIC was already showing 'Apply now! Academic year 2026/27 - Application period has ended' in a 6 February 2026 snapshot, consistent with the 29 January 2026 closing date. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: No standardised entrance examination (no TOLC, no GRE/GMAT, no SAT). Admission is decided by an INTERVIEW conducted in English by a member of the AGIC Selection Committee (named in the 2025/2026 official page as Prof. Bignante, Prof. Bobbio, Prof. Borgnino, Prof. Gusman and Prof. Romano). Candidates who already hold the curricular requirements are split into two streams: (a) candidates with at least 24 CFU across at least 3 of the listed SSD blocks AND a bachelor's final mark of at least 99/110 (or, if not yet graduated, an exam average of at least 26/30) sit a motivational interview only; (b) all other candidates sit an interview that also tests their knowledge of a booklet ('opuscolo') prepared by the AGIC lecturers and published in the 'How to Apply' section of the AGIC website. In both streams the interview also assesses English and the second language. Candidates with a foreign qualification are admitted to the same English-language interview, which assesses English and the second language (which for international students may be Italian) and discusses general knowledge of the main themes of the programme and previous experience. Historical note: for a.y. 2023/2024 candidates with Italian qualifications first had to pass an ONLINE WRITTEN TEST on Moodle/Webex (30 minutes, max 300-word critical comment on a short text or a map/graph/chart) before the interview, and in 2020 international candidates sat a 20-question multiple-choice written test on selected entries of 'The Development Dictionary' (ed. W. Sachs). The 2025/2026 and cohort-2026 official texts describe only an interview, so the written test appears to have been dropped, but this could not be confirmed on a live 2026/2027 page. [uncertain]
academic_requirements:
1) QUALIFICATION: a Bachelor's Degree ('Laurea Triennale') or a three-year university diploma, or any qualification obtained abroad recognised as equivalent under the legislation in force. The apply.unito.it entry-qualification statement requires a first-cycle degree gained after at least 3 years of university education.
2) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS - the candidate must satisfy ONE of the following: (a) an Italian degree in Political Science and International Relations (class L-36); (b) an Italian degree in Peace Studies (class L-37); or (c) at least 18 Italian credits (CFU/ECTS or equivalent) spread across AT LEAST TWO of the listed blocks of academic disciplines (SSD). The blocks are summarised on apply.unito.it as: Law; History, Anthropology, Demography; Economics, Statistics; Political sciences, Social sciences; Language and translation (French, Portuguese, Spanish, Swahili, Arabic, Hindi, Chinese, Russian). The detailed SSD list includes L-LIN/04, L-LIN/06, L-LIN/07, L-LIN/09, L-LIN/12, L-OR/09, L-OR/10, L-OR/12, L-OR/19, L-OR/21, IUS/02, IUS/08, IUS/09, IUS/13, IUS/14, IUS/21, M-DEA/01, M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02, M-STO/02, M-STO/03, M-STO/04, M-STO/05, M-STO/06, SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/12, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, SECS-S/05, SPS/02, SPS/03, SPS/04, SPS/05, SPS/06, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, SPS/12, SPS/13, SPS/14. If the applicant already holds an Italian Master's degree, the credit count is made over the whole university career.
3) PERSONAL PREPARATION: verified through the mandatory admission interview; enrolment is not permitted where a 'carenza formativa' (training deficit) exists.
4) GPA / GRADE THRESHOLD: there is no minimum grade for admission as such, but a grade threshold determines the interview stream - a final bachelor's mark of at least 99/110, or an exam average of at least 26/30 for not-yet-graduated candidates, combined with at least 24 CFU in at least 3 SSD blocks, places the candidate in the lighter 'motivational interview only' stream.
5) IT SKILLS: an adequate ability to use the main IT tools (word processing, spreadsheets, design and management of databases, presentation tools) is assumed.
6) PLACES / QUOTAS: the programme is not capped for the general pool ('accesso non programmato'). Reserved quotas: 60 places for non-EU citizens residing abroad (stated on apply.unito.it as 'Territory requirements') and 10 places for Marco Polo programme students.
7) CANDIDATES WITHOUT THE CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS: on a resolution of the degree-programme board (CCLM) they may enrol in single courses ('corsi singoli') offered by the University and must pass the corresponding assessments before enrolling in the Master's; in every case enrolment remains conditional on passing the personal-preparation interview.
8) FOREIGN-QUALIFICATION HOLDERS may register only through the University's procedures for international students (Apply@UniTo); possession of the curricular requirements is verified by the Commission for the Admission of International Students. [uncertain]
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - CEFR B2 or higher is required. Two routes are accepted at application through Apply@UniTo: (i) an international certificate no more than three years old, from the accepted list with minimum scores - Cambridge CPE; Cambridge CAE; Cambridge FCE with minimum score 173 (grade B); PTE Academic minimum 65; IELTS minimum 5.5 overall with no component below 5.5; TOEFL iBT minimum 69/120 with no component below 17; Trinity College ISE II; or (ii) an official document issued by the applicant's previous university stating that the medium of instruction was English. The programme's own admission page adds that students may self-certify adequate English by presenting a university English exam certificate equivalent to the required level. English is also assessed orally during the admission interview, which is conducted in English.
SECOND LANGUAGE - a basic knowledge (CEFR A2 or higher) of ONE of the other languages taught in the Master's programme is required: French, Portuguese, Spanish, Swahili, Arabic, Hindi, Chinese, Russian, Japanese (apply.unito.it adds Italian to this list for international applicants). This can be self-certified by presenting a university language exam certificate at the equivalent level, and it is verified during the interview.
ITALIAN - foreign students are required to have a basic knowledge of Italian (A2 or higher); those who do not have it must take an Italian course for international students (at UNITO or elsewhere). Note that the UNITO-wide rule requiring a CLIQ-issued B2 Italian certificate by the Universitaly deadline applies only to Italian-taught undergraduate / 5-6-year programmes, so it does NOT apply to this English-taught master's; the A2 Italian expectation here is a programme-level requirement, and the official Italian-language text of the access requirements says the interview for international candidates verifies knowledge of English AND Italian. [uncertain]
tuition_or_fees_link: https://en.unito.it/studying-unito/tuition-fees (this is the link used by the AGIC microsite's own 'Tuition fees' menu item; the dedicated international page is https://en.unito.it/studying-unito/tuition-fees/tuition-fees-international-students). A separate non-refundable EUR 60 application fee applies. Figures for a.y. 2026-27 are to be checked on the University portal.

uncertainty_notes:
SOURCE ACCESS LIMITATION: the AGIC microsite (www.agic.unito.it) is currently unreachable for automated fetching - direct HTTPS connections are refused (ECONNREFUSED 130.186.3.24:443) and a rendering proxy timed out on it. apply.unito.it and en.unito.it return HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to direct WebFetch. Content above was reconstructed from three working channels: (1) a rendering proxy that succeeded on the LIVE apply.unito.it course page 468 and the LIVE en.unito.it pages (degree record 0308M23 and the international-application page), which are therefore first-hand and current; (2) Wayback Machine captures of the AGIC microsite - admission_requirements.html captured 18 October 2025 (page content stamped 'Academic Year 2025/2026', last update 19/05/2025), how_to_apply.html captured 28 September 2023 (content for a.y. 2023/2024), and the apply.unito.it course page captured 6 February 2026; (3) search-engine indexed extracts for the AGIC key_information.html page, which could not be retrieved directly in any recent version.

SPECIFIC OPEN POINTS:
1) Programme scope is clear: AGIC is a full standalone English-taught Laurea Magistrale (2 years, 120 ECTS, LM-81 R), not a pathway inside an Italian-named degree and not an interuniversity/joint degree. This is corroborated by en.unito.it, apply.unito.it, the CPS department list and the CINECA catalogue.
2) 2026/2027 ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS PAGE: the most recent retrievable version of the AGIC admission-requirements page is headed 'Academic Year 2025/2026'. However, the en.unito.it official degree record for cohort 2026 (annoOrdinamento=2026) reproduces substantively the same access requirements in Italian, so the requirements are believed to be unchanged for 2026/2027. UNITO's own pages carry the caveat 'Information for the a.y. 2026-2027 being updated'.
3) WRITTEN TEST vs INTERVIEW: earlier cycles used a written test (a 20-question multiple-choice test on 'The Development Dictionary' in 2020; a 30-minute online 300-word commentary test on Moodle/Webex for a.y. 2023/2024 for Italian-qualification candidates) followed by an interview. The 2025/2026 and cohort-2026 official texts describe an INTERVIEW ONLY, with the 'booklet' knowledge check folded into the interview for stream (b) candidates. The written test therefore appears to have been discontinued, but this could not be confirmed on a live 2026/2027 page.
4) INTERVIEW SESSION DATES for 2026/2027 (registration windows through MyUniTo for Italian-qualification candidates, and scheduling for Apply@UniTo candidates) could not be retrieved; the 'How to apply' page that publishes them is unreachable. The 2023/2024 pattern was three sessions (June, July, September) plus an October make-up session strictly reserved to candidates who had failed.
5) ADMISSION CALL NUMBERING CONFLICT: apply.unito.it labels the 25 August - 8 September 2026 window the 'Fourth admission call for open access postgraduate degree programs only', whereas en.unito.it labels the same dates the 'Second application call for free access postgraduate programs'. The dates agree; only the numbering differs. Both agree the window is reserved to Italians, EU citizens, EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy - so non-EU applicants residing abroad had only the 25 Nov 2025 - 29 Jan 2026 window for 2026/2027.
6) QUOTA FIGURES: the 60 non-EU places figure is confirmed first-hand on apply.unito.it. The additional '10 places reserved for Marco Polo students' comes only from a search-engine extract of the AGIC key_information.html page and could not be verified against the live page.
7) ITALIAN LANGUAGE: the programme requires international students to have basic Italian (A2) or take an Italian course, and the Italian text of the access requirements says the interview for international candidates verifies English AND Italian - while the AGIC English page says the interview verifies English and 'second language (which in the case of international students can be Italian, too)'. Whether A2 Italian is a hard admission bar or a post-admission expectation is not fully clear; the English wording ('Those who don't have this level of Italian must take an Italian course') suggests it is not blocking.
8) TUITION: no programme-specific fee page exists; UNITO applies a university-wide income-based scheme. The EUR 156-2,800 range is the officially quoted 2025-26 range on apply.unito.it; 2026-27 figures were not published on any page that could be retrieved, and UNITO is transitioning international students from ISEE Parificato to a scale based on GDP per capita (PPP) of the country of residence.
9) CAMPUS: 'TORINO' is the official headquarter. The specific teaching site (Campus Luigi Einaudi, home of the Department of Cultures, Politics and Society) is inferred from the department affiliation rather than stated on a retrieved AGIC page.
10) Per task scope, no polito.it sources were used; all sources are unito.it domains plus Wayback Machine captures of unito.it pages.
